title: Where delivery exists, delivery state must be inspectable independently from discovery/review state
requirement: If a Clank has any mechanism that delivers items to an external channel (Discord, webhook, or equivalent) and that mechanism records its own outcome (sent/failed/pending/suppressed or equivalent), the UI MUST make that delivery outcome independently inspectable, separate from whether the item was merely discovered or QC-reviewed. This does NOT require a dedicated Delivery page — a tab, a drawer, an outbox panel, a section within an event/item detail view, or a dedicated route all satisfy this, as long as an operator can distinguish discovery/review state from delivery state. Collapsing multiple distinct delivery outcomes into one ambiguous indicator (e.g. a single boolean that cannot distinguish 'sent' from 'pending' from 'suppressed' from 'failed') does not satisfy this. A Clank with no delivery mechanism at all, or one that has explicitly and honestly disabled delivery, is out of scope — not a violation.
rationale: Genuinely cross-family, independently-evidenced pattern: chinese-tech-wire (news), semiconductor-intelligence (news/specialist), and smartphone-clank (SKU) each independently built a dedicated delivery-inspection surface with real per-outcome granularity (SENT/FAILED/DRY_RUN/SUPPRESSED/POLICY_ACTIVATED with http_status/error_text in CTW; a dedicated External Delivery card with preview/test/enable controls in semiconductor-intelligence; per-channel Configured/Last-attempted/Last-delivered plus Eligible/Attempted/Delivered/Suppressed/Failed counts and a Recent-failures table in smartphone-clank, arguably the best implementation in the fleet). Counter-evidence is equally concrete and instructive: watch-clank and feature-phone-clank both compute and persist real delivery outcomes in their backends but never read that data in any template (confirmed by grep, zero references) — the data exists and is simply not surfaced. oem-radar has genuine per-item delivery states in its database but its dashboard collapses pending and sent into a single 'notified' boolean, and failed/suppressed items render with no badge at all, making them visually indistinguishable from items that were never processed for delivery — an actively misleading gap, not just an absent feature.
forbidden: Computing and persisting a real delivery outcome and never exposing it anywhere in the GUI
A single 'notified'/'delivered' boolean that cannot distinguish sent from pending, and renders failed/suppressed identically to never-attempted
acceptance: If delivery outcomes are tracked in the backend, an operator can see, per item or per channel, which distinct outcome applies (not just yes/no)
A failed or suppressed delivery is visually distinguishable from an item that was never eligible for delivery

evidence.summary: Dedicated Alerts nav tab, filterable by outcome, with http_status/error_text.
Per-channel and per-message delivery visibility with a Recent-failures sub-table; arguably the fleet's best implementation, on a SKU-family Clank.
Dedicated External Delivery card, separate from discovery/review filters, on a news/specialist Clank.

evidence.source: watch-clank/app/main.py:1965-1966 (alerted flag never read by any template); feature-phone-clank/providers/discord/__init__.py:114-194 (notifications table with documented 'even a suppressed event gets a row' design, never referenced by dashboard.py)
evidence.summary: Two Clanks compute and persist real delivery outcomes that are never surfaced in the GUI at all.
Real pending/sent/failed/suppressed states exist in the notifications table but the dashboard collapses pending+sent into one 'notified' boolean and shows no badge at all for failed/suppressed items.

notes: RATIFIED 2026-08-30 by Operator Ratification Decision 002 (decisions/0004-operator-ratification-decision-002.md). Version 2: requirement text made explicit that no dedicated Delivery page is required — a tab, drawer, outbox panel, or event-detail section all conform, matching CTW's/semiconductor-intelligence's/smartphone-clank's differing-but-conforming shapes. Out of scope, not a violation: korean-tech-wire (no delivery mechanism exists at all) and tablet-clank (delivery architecturally stripped and explicitly labeled 'delivery disabled'). smartwatch-clank has an unwired discord module in its source tree with no clear disable statement — flagged as ambiguous rather than confidently scoped in or out.
